correctness.rationale: For every n even >=6 and h>0, all generic section vertices correspond bijectively to prism edges with opposite signs. On a basic azimuth sector, the two largest distinct absolute projected base-vertex coordinates are cos(theta) and cos(2pi/n-theta). Exactly n+2 crossings occur iff the normalized vertical tilt is strictly between those two thresholds. Uniformity of azimuth and |U_z| integrates this event into an exact two-arcsine formula, with positivity on every interior h>0. Differentiation yields a sole sign change when 1+h^2=3cos^2(pi/n), giving the unique interior global maximizer. Exact Taylor series prove the sharp optimal n^-2 and edge-uniform n^-4 probabilities. The included checker verifies angular threshold equivalence against 210,000 independent geometric edge counts, exact special cases and direct quadrature. These finite checks corroborate; only the algebraic reasoning proves all parameters.

value.rationale: The probability of the maximal possible n+2 section sides is the most discriminating upper-tail polygon-type invariant of a central cut. Its exact distribution across height determines a non-obvious unique aspect-ratio optimum for every even regular n>=6, including the first hexagonal-prism benchmark. The theorem proves an asymptotic n^-2 optimal chance versus an n^-4 chance for the familiar uniform prism, a growing quadratic separation with geometric significance. It answers a complete natural infinite-family question rather than a mere cubic relabeling or insignificant numerical increment.
